summary: Splits one stereo input into four outputs that add up to the input, each wired to its own chain. Bands: two, three or four frequency bands on Linkwitz–Riley crossovers (24 or 48 dB/oct) whose bands sum flat; Transient and Body: the onsets on output 1 and what is left on output 2, found by two followers of the level with a 2 ms lookahead; Mid and Side: the centre on output 1 and the difference on output 2, so that the two add up to left and right. It only routes: there is no Mix or Amount, and the outputs summed are the input (Bands: flat in level, the phase turned by the crossovers' allpass). Use it for parallel processing: a different chain for the lows and the highs, the hits and the tails, or the middle and the sides.
use_for: One input, four outputs that add up to it: frequency bands, transients and body, or mid and side, each output to its own chain for parallel processing.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: What is split: frequency bands, the transients and the body, or mid and side (the outputs are named Out 1 to Out 4; what each carries depends on the mode)
parameters.how: Chooses what the input is split into: frequency bands, transients and body, or mid and side.
parameters.sound: Bands gives each range of the spectrum its own output, Transient and Body separates the hit from what follows it, and Mid and Side separates the centre from the width.

parameters.name: Bands
parameters.description: How many frequency bands (Bands mode): 2, 3 or 4. The outputs after the last band are silent
parameters.how: Chooses how many frequency bands the input is split into: 2, 3 or 4.
parameters.sound: More bands let more chains work on separate ranges; the bands always add up to the input.

parameters.name: Slope
parameters.description: The steepness of each crossover (Bands mode): Linkwitz–Riley 24 dB/oct, or 48 dB/oct for a narrow overlap. Each band is 6 dB down at its crossover and the bands sum flat
parameters.how: Chooses how sharply each crossover separates the bands: 24 or 48 dB per octave.
parameters.sound: 24 dB/oct is the classic, gentle overlap; 48 dB/oct keeps the bands apart, which suits treating a band hard, at a little more ringing near the crossover.

parameters.name: Crossover 1
parameters.description: Between the first and the second band (never closer than a third of an octave to the next crossover)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the first and second band, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
parameters.sound: It decides how much of the low end the first output gets.

parameters.name: Crossover 2
parameters.description: Between the second and the third band (kept at least a third of an octave above Crossover 1)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the second and third band.
parameters.sound: It moves the boundary between the lower and upper midrange.

parameters.name: Crossover 3
parameters.description: Between the third and the fourth band (kept at least a third of an octave above Crossover 2)
parameters.how: Sets the frequency between the third and fourth band.
parameters.sound: It decides where the top band begins.

parameters.name: Sensitivity
parameters.description: Transient and Body mode: how easily a rise in level counts as a transient (0 % only the sharpest hits, 100 % every swell)
parameters.how: Sets how large a rise in level must be to count as a transient.
parameters.sound: Low values send only the hardest hits to Out 1; high values send smaller attacks and swells too.

parameters.name: Transient length
parameters.description: Transient and Body mode: how long after an onset the sound still counts as the transient (the detector's followers: 2 to 100 ms)
parameters.how: Sets how long a hit's attack lasts, from 2 to 100 ms.
parameters.sound: Short values keep only the click of a hit on Out 1; long values carry the first part of the note with it.

parameters.name: Body smoothing
parameters.description: Transient and Body mode: how slowly the body comes back after a transient (the transient's weight falls over this time; 0 is at once)
parameters.how: Sets how slowly the body returns after a transient, from 0 to 100 ms.
parameters.sound: Short values give a clean cut between transient and body; long values leave the start of the tail with the transient and make the body fade in.

readings.description: Peak level of output 1 over the last block, in dBFS (−120 when silent)
The delay of every output: 0 in Bands and Mid and Side, the 2 ms lookahead in Transient and Body (reported to NeoBuzz Live)
